summary: Reviewed onCheckoutCompleted's corrected isRetryOfSameCheckout guard and its two new tests. (1) session.subscription null/undefined fails open (!!session.subscription short-circuits to false), so notifications still fire rather than being silently swallowed -- fail-safe, not fail-silent. (2) True concurrent redelivery of the SAME Stripe event is already deduped upstream by recordWebhookProcessed's ON CONFLICT(stripe_event_id) DO NOTHING before onCheckoutCompleted is ever reached, so the TOCTOU window between subBefore's read and the UPDATE only matters across genuinely distinct events (real successive checkouts for the same org), where reading a stale subBefore just makes both look like non-retries -- correct, not a false suppression. (3) Traced both new jest tests line-by-line against the shared mockDs._repo._qb.getOne mock: test 1 sets one getOne() resolution (stripe_sub_id/plan/status all matching) and the code path returns before any second getOne() call, matching the single mock; test 2 sets two sequential resolutions (first mismatched plan -> isRetry=false -> code proceeds to a second getOne() for tenantRecord) matching its two mocks. Reverting the fix (dropping subBefore for org.billing_status) would fail test 2 (org already active by the time of a real upgrade) while still passing test 1, confirming the tests exercise the actual differentiating logic, not a coincidental green. (4) No dangling orgBefore reference, no unused imports; TenantBillingStatus and StripeCheckoutSession are both actively used. Two LOW findings filed for the record (find-ce4d9c15: org_id has no unique DB constraint on billing_subscriptions so subBefore's getOne() is not provably the right row if a duplicate org_id row ever exists -- a pre-existing systemic assumption also relied on by getSubscription, not newly introduced; find-a62976af: the guard doesn't yet distinguish 'DB write applied' from 'side effects already delivered', so a crash between the write and TENANT_CREATED still permanently swallows that notification on retry -- this failure mode predates this round and is not a regression). Neither finding is a regression from this specific fix and neither reopens the originally reported plan-upgrade-suppression bug, which is correctly fixed. Wave 5 (Billing/Stripe) has no other open blocking finding to my knowledge from this file.
